title: Chick Webb's tuning and Leeman's piccolo snare
summary: Leeman says Chick Webb and Catlett tuned drums for a high sound, which led him to prefer a four-inch deep piccolo snare.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: As I told you before, knowing and listening to Chick Webb play helped me to model some of my ideas. He tuned his drums. Sidney Catlett, too, about the same way, with opened and dampened heads, and got a high sound. Chick Webb's was predominantly on the soloist's side, and it was just so wonderful, you had to hear them. There weren't enough recordings of his, and of course, they were very technical -- I mean, they were full of technique, is what I should say, swinging technically.

And I adapted to tuning my drums along those lines, and still adhere to those sounds today. I can't stand a deep snare drum's tone. That's why I use a three and a half, or at the most, a four-inch deep snare. I like the four-inch by 13-inch in diameter, the so-called piccolo snare drum in my work -- I've been using it for a long time for a crisp sound.
